description: Volatility clustering: OLS slope of |idx_ret[t+1]| on |idx_ret[t]| (idx = EW daily simple return of the universe)
cost_note: not a trade; volatility clustering is the premise of W3.2/W3.3
notes: mean |idx_ret| MAIN 99 bps; autocorrelation of |idx_ret| lag1 0.24, lag5 0.19, lag20 0.11; idx rebuilt from pre2018 tickers for pre2018; with the artefact days (idx_n < 10, incl. the +20.06% Saturday 2009-06-06 single-CTRA bar) zeroed the MAIN slope is 0.255 (t 9.1); survivorship low: index-level volatility persistence does not depend much on which stocks survived

description: 20-day realised idx vol (std of idx_ret t-19..t) in its top tercile minus bottom tercile (expanding thresholds up to t, >= 500 values; middle excluded); forward EW mean fo[20] (Open t+1 -> Close t+20)
cost_note: timing: analog rule (cash in the regime with the lower MAIN forward return, so its direction is chosen in-sample) cash_when_vol_bottom_tercile (open exec, cost B): CAGR 7.3% vs always-in 22.9%, Sharpe 0.45 vs 1.03, MDD -57% vs -62%, exposure 0.50, 9.0 changes/yr; verdict: worse than always-in after cost B [dCAGR -15.6 pp/yr, dSharpe -0.57, dMDD +5.0 pp, positive dMDD = shallower]; Sharpe higher than always-in after B in 0 of 4 subperiods; cost A: worse than always-in after cost A [dCAGR -13.2 pp/yr, dSharpe -0.46, dMDD +5.7 pp, positive dMDD = shallower]; opposite rule: cash_when_vol_top_tercile (open exec, cost B): CAGR 13.9% vs always-in 22.9%, Sharpe 0.82 vs 1.03, MDD -69% vs -62%, exposure 0.86, 4.0 changes/yr
notes: MAIN days top tercile 891 / bottom tercile 3087 (51 separate top tercile spells); mean forward return top tercile +1.88% vs bottom tercile +0.92% (raw EW, overlapping windows); with only 51 spells of a persistent regime the effective sample is far smaller than the day count, so the NW t may overstate the evidence; dropping any one MAIN year leaves +0.36% (without 2009) to +1.87% (without 2008), t 0.31 to 2.07; the within-year difference has the MAIN sign in 12 of 19 MAIN years with both regimes, so the pooled effect also reflects differences between years and a few long episodes (by_year, loyo in context); survivorship high: idx and forward returns are built from today's Kompas100 members (EW idx level x513 from 1994-07 to 2025-08), so stocks that crashed and were delisted or dropped are missing; that bias is largest right after crashes; this effect favours buying the turbulent regime, exactly where survivors rebounded

description: Vol targeting: exposure min(1.5, expanding median(sigma20)/sigma20[t]) on idx_ret[t+1] vs constant exposure 1; annualised Sharpe difference (t column = paired 20-day block bootstrap z, 2,000 resamples)

notes: MAIN gross (PLAN convention, close exec, no cost): Sharpe 1.19 vs 1.03, MDD -60% vs -62%, CAGR 27.1% vs 22.9%, mean exposure 1.17; bootstrap sd 0.098, 95% interval [-0.02, +0.36]; t column = bootstrap z; ANN 242.9 market days per year; per-period Sharpe and MDD of both in context; survivorship low: idx and forward returns are built from today's Kompas100 members (EW idx level x513 from 1994-07 to 2025-08), so stocks that crashed and were delisted or dropped are missing; that bias is largest right after crashes; vol targeting cuts exposure after crashes, when survivors rebounded, so the bias works against vol targeting

description: Lead-lag: OLS slope of small-cap EW fo[1] at row t (bottom tercile of 60-day mean traded value, sorted monthly; Open->Close of t+1) on large-cap (top tercile) EW r_cc of day t
cost_note: filter for small-cap entries at the next Open: next-day Open->Close of small caps after large-cap up days minus down days +6.6 bps (t 1.89) vs filter threshold 25 bps -> below; a standalone day trade would need > 0.90% (B) / 0.40% (A) per round trip
notes: slope x 1% large-cap move = +1.2 bps next-day small-cap Open->Close; the same regression on the small caps' overnight gap into t+1 gives slope 0.094 (t 6.4) and close-to-close 0.107 (t 5.7) (X-W3.7-on/-cc): the lead-lag that exists is mostly in the gap before the next Open, which an entry at the Open cannot capture; median stocks per tercile MAIN small 22 / large 21; the month-end sort applies from the next row (same-row sort and controls in context); survivorship medium: the small tercile holds the least liquid current members, whose history is the most survivor-selected
